name: Infosys (SE, DSE, Specialist Programmer)
tagline: From System Engineer to Specialist Programmer and Power Programmer

overview.about: Infosys hires freshers mainly as System Engineer (SE), Digital Specialist Engineer (DSE) and Specialist Programmer (SP). The highest-pay Power Programmer route usually comes through the HackWithInfy coding contest. SE uses an aptitude + pseudo-code test; DSE/SP use a harder coding-heavy assessment. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.
eligibility: Typically 60% or more (or equivalent CGPA) throughout, no active backlogs at joining (as reported)
HackWithInfy is open to engineering students of the batches announced for that edition

pattern.note: Easy, medium, hard; sectional cut-offs reported
Technical + HR; deeper DSA for SP/DSE

overview.frequency: Campus drives each season; HackWithInfy usually once a year

chapters.title: Roles and the SE online test

cards.title: Three main fresher roles
points: System Engineer (SE): entry role, aptitude + pseudo-code test
Digital Specialist Engineer (DSE): higher band, coding-heavy test
Specialist Programmer (SP) / Power Programmer: highest band, strong DSA needed

cards.title: SE test sections
cards.body: Logical reasoning, mathematical ability, verbal ability, pseudo-code and puzzle solving, each with sectional timing. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Mathematical ability is the filter
cards.body: Infosys maths is a notch above typical service-company quant: number theory, P&C, probability, geometry and functions. Practise accuracy over speed.

cards.title: Sample: mathematical ability
cards.body:
Q: How many positive divisors does 360 have?
360 = 2³ × 3² × 5 → (3+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 24.

cards.title: Sample: pseudo-code
cards.body:
x = 0
for i = 1 to 10
  if i mod 3 == 0: x = x + i
print x
→ 3 + 6 + 9 = 18

cards.title: Puzzle solving
cards.body: Logic grids, arrangement puzzles and 'who is lying' questions. Draw a table; eliminate impossible cells first.

cards.q:
s = 1
for i = 1 to 4
  s = s * i
print s — output?

cards.title: Format
cards.body: As reported: 3 problems in about 3 hours — usually one easy, one medium and one hard. Partial scores per test case. Cut-offs apply, so the easy problem must be fully solved.

cards.title: Common topics
points: Strings, bit manipulation, binary search on the answer

cards.title: HackWithInfy
cards.body: Infosys's national coding contest for engineering students. Top performers get interview opportunities for SP/Power Programmer roles plus prizes. Registration is announced on the Infosys careers site.

cards.title: Sample-style problem
cards.body:
Given n tasks with deadlines and profits, schedule one task per unit time to maximise profit.
Idea: sort by profit (desc), place each task in the latest free slot ≤ its deadline (greedy, O(n log n) with DSU).

cards.title: Partial marks matter
cards.body: If the hard problem is out of reach, write a brute force that passes small test cases. Every passed test case counts.

cards.title: Preparation plan
cards.body: Solve ~100 medium and ~30 hard problems across DP, graphs and greedy on a free judge, timing yourself to 45 minutes per medium problem.

cards.q: In a 3-problem, 3-hour coding test, the best opening move is usually:
options: Fully solve the easiest problem first
Write all three solutions without testing
cards.explain: Securing the easy problem clears cut-offs and builds time for the rest.

cards.q: Job sequencing with deadlines is typically solved by:
options: Greedy: sort by profit, fill latest free slot
cards.explain: Taking the most profitable jobs first and scheduling them as late as possible is optimal.

cards.title: Technical interview (SE)
cards.body: Basics of one language, OOP, DBMS queries, simple programs (prime, palindrome, Fibonacci), and your project. Clarity matters more than breadth.

cards.title: Technical interview (DSE/SP)
cards.body: Live DSA problem-solving with complexity analysis, follow-ups on your coding-round solution, CS fundamentals in depth and sometimes basic system design.

cards.title: HR round
cards.body: Self-introduction, relocation readiness, interest in Infosys, strengths and weaknesses. Keep answers honest and concise.

cards.title: Training at Mysuru
cards.body: Selected freshers usually go through foundation training at the Infosys Global Education Centre, Mysuru, followed by assessments. Taking training seriously matters for project allocation.

cards.title: Explain your coding-round solution
cards.body: Interviewers often open your test submission. Be ready to explain your approach, its complexity and how you'd improve it.

cards.title: Common SE question
cards.body: "Write a program to check whether a string is a palindrome without using reverse()." → two pointers from both ends; mention O(n) time, O(1) space.

cards.q: For a DSE/SP interview, which preparation is most important?
options: DSA problem solving with complexity analysis

cards.q: Time complexity of the two-pointer palindrome check:
cards.explain: Each character is compared at most once.
